??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Welcome, *Player*. Here is a riddle for the threshold: what comes in without a key, leaves without a word, and is always being asked the price? You. Customers.
    - *Player*! The opener of doors, or at least the carrier of news about them. Leland sends word that the iron door swings like a garden gate now. Mine is the only door on the Row with no handle, and I intend to keep it that way.
    - *Player*. The owl sits on my shelf and watches me work. Too clever for its buyer, the note said. Too clever for its maker too, for twenty-eight years. I have not stopped grinning.
    - Ask, and I may answer. Buy, and I certainly will.
        - *Choice:* How do your boxes open?
        - *Choice:* Where did you learn locks?
        - *Choice:* What is that walnut box on the shelf?
        - *Choice:* Nothing today.
    - How does a song open? In the right order, or not at all. Taps and turns, presses and slides, sometimes a breath on the right corner. Every box has its tune.
    - I write every sequence in a book now. The book is locked in another box. The box's sequence I keep in my head. You see the weakness. So do I. I enjoy it.
    - I swept for Esmond the locksmith from the age of twelve. He said a lock is a promise and a good one is a joke. When he died I kept the shop and took the handle off the door. Velvet sells my smaller boxes in the Night Market, and tells stories about them that are better than the truth.
    - Ah. You found the embarrassment. Dark walnut, a brass key-shaped inlay on every face and no keyhole anywhere. I made it about twenty-eight years ago and sold it at the Night Market to a traveller whose face I cannot recall.
    - It came back this spring with a carter, unopened, and a note: the buyer could not solve it. Neither can I. I have forgotten my own trick. Something rattles inside, and it is laughing at me.
    - Open, at last, thanks to a bucket drummer and you. Inside: a little wooden owl and a note in my own young hand. I keep the box open on the shelf as a warning to myself about cleverness.
    - Mind the door on your way out. It has no handle, so it will not mind you.
